Everything above about "50X The Cash" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
981.headline: A close look at the prizes

985.body:
Of the unclaimed prize money on "MAX-A-MILLION", most is in wins under $5,000. The game is a game with most of its money in small, frequent prizes. That is neither good nor bad, only how it was designed. Choose the kind of game that fits the win you want.

The numbers for "MAX-A-MILLION" are recalculated every morning, and this page changes with them.
985.headline: The prize mix in this game

988.body:
The prize money on "Emerald 10's" leans toward small, frequent prizes. It is spread over eleven prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $1 million. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

Everything above about "Emerald 10's" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
988.headline: How this game pays out

990.body:
About three-quarters of the tickets for "LADY LUCK" are sold. The top prize count has held, with two of four still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

Every line of LADY LUCK's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
990.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

992.body:
The key fact about "$2 MILLION VAULT" is how its twelve prize levels are built. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games built like this give out wins often, but rarely large ones. Prize counts change daily, but this design does not.

If you play "$2 MILLION VAULT" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.
992.headline: Same price, different prizes

993.body:
"$5,000 Triple Play" has gone five months without a top prize claim, and tickets kept selling. Only a fixed number of tickets are printed. About three-quarters of the tickets are sold, and every remaining $5,000 prize is still unclaimed. That leaves the same top prizes among fewer tickets.

Every line of $5,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
993.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

994.body:
"$25,000 Triple Play" has 111,591 prizes of $2 still unclaimed, which is its most common win. Just below the top prize is the $3,000 prize, with three left. The full count for every prize level is listed below.

Every line of $25,000 Triple Play's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
994.headline: Prize table details

995.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "$200,000 Triple Play" have been sold. The game is past the halfway point of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

If "$200,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
995.headline: How far along this game is

996.body:
The top prize count on "$1,000,000 Triple Play" has not moved since we started watching it. The game still has four of five top prizes unclaimed. Smaller prizes keep getting claimed as tickets sell. The same top prizes are now among fewer tickets.

If "$1,000,000 Triple Play" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
996.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed
